title: Tenant-aware staged upgrade scheduler and capacity reservation coordinator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Upgrading dedicated GPU pools currently risks capacity loss and request surges because drains and autoscaler handoffs are not coordinated across tenant affinity boundaries or LTS channel semantics. We need a scheduler that stages node drains while reserving tenant capacity, respects LTS/patch channels, and gates per-tenant rollouts to preserve SLAs for high-priority customers.

Goals: 
- Minimize request errors and latency spikes during pool upgrades for Dedicated customers.
- Preserve predictable throughput for P0/P1 tenants by reserving capacity and pre-warming alternative paths.
- Support LTS channels and per-tenant rollout gates so upgrades can be applied to a subset of customers first.
- Integrate with existing autoscaler so scaling decisions do not counteract drain progress.
- Provide observability (per-tenant capacity ledger, drain progress, gating state) and automated rollback triggers.

Design overview: 
1) Staggered Upgrade Intent (SUI): a controller that receives an upgrade manifest (target runtime version + channel tag e.g., lts-2026-03) and computes a tenant-aware sequence of drain windows. Tenants are bucketed by priority and tenancy density on each GPU pool node.

2) Capacity Reservation Ledger: before draining a node, SUI creates a short-lived reservation token for tenant slots equal to the load expected to shift off the draining node. The ledger is consulted by the autoscaler as a hint to avoid scaling down capacity that SUI intends to occupy during the upgrade. Reservations are best-effort and have TTLs.

3) Autoscaler handshake protocol: We extend the autoscaler with a lightweight two-way handshake: SUI requests an evict window; autoscaler replies with occupancy projection and a suggested pause-or-throttle decision. If autoscaler suggests pause, SUI reorders windows to reduce concurrent drains that would cause surge.

4) Rollout Gates + LTS semantics: The manifest can include a rollout policy which references LTS channels and per-tenant allowlists/deny-lists. Gate checks occur at the tenant and region granularity. Canary audience is defined as a percent of nodes and explicit tenant IDs.

5) Safe fallback: A monitoring rule watches per-tenant 95th/99th latency, error rate, dropped connection rate, and provisioned capacity usage. If thresholds breach (configurable per-tenant), SUI will abort new drains, and trigger immediate re-schedule or automated rollback for nodes in current wave.

APIs and artifacts: 
- Upgrade manifest format: /api/v1/upgrade-manifests POST (schema attached in design doc link).
- Reservation API: /internal/reservations POST/DELETE/GET for ledger state.
- Handshake: autoscaler exposes /internal/handshake?v=1 which returns projection and decision.

Telemetry and dashboards: 
- New Grafana: "Upgrade Coordinator -> Per-pool ledger" dashboard (per-tenant reservation usage, pending drains, wave health).
- SLO monitors: per-tenant latency/error panels and alert rules.
- Audit log for manifest changes and gate overrides.

Runbook (high level): 
- Preflight: run manifest validation and dry-run mode that simulates reservation outcomes and autoscaler responses (dry-run produces expected capacity curve).
- Start wave: SUI marks nodes in wave, creates reservations, signals autoscaler handshake, and initiates node drain.
- Monitor: watch metrics; on soft breach (warning) pause new waves; on hard breach (critical) stop drains and run rollback.
- Post-upgrade: release reservations and emit final report with per-tenant impact metrics.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Strong reservations vs. reuse of free capacity: strong reservations reduce risk but may increase temporary costs and block background jobs. We chose TTL-limited reservations and per-tenant caps to balance.
- Centralized coordinator vs. distributed agents: centralized SUI simplifies sequencing and observability; risk: single-point-of-control. Mitigation: make SUI leader-elected with hot standby and persistent manifest state.

Testing plan: 
- Unit: reservation TTL expiry, ledger conflict resolution, handshake error modes.
- Integration: staging cluster end-to-end with synthetic tenant traffic and adjustable autoscaler sensitivity.
- Chaos: induce autoscaler flaps and node failures while running mid-wave drains.
- Canaries: roll to a 2% tenant cohort for 48h before broad waves.

Success metrics: 
- 99.9% of requests served (no increase in 5xx) during upgrade windows for P0 tenants.
- No more than 10% increase in p95 latency for P1 tenants during upgrades.
- Reduction in manual rollback incidents caused by capacity storms vs. previous quarter.

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Exact per-tenant reservation sizing algorithm (simple 95th -> conservative multiplier vs. ML-based prediction).
- Autoscaler policy change scope required to honor reservations in multi-tenant signals.
- UI: whether to expose per-tenant progress in Console or keep in internal ops tools.

Links to artifacts: 
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/SUI+Design+Doc
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/5123
- Simulation results (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/sim/upgrade-sim-2026-03

Next milestones: 
- 2026-03-20: complete autoscaler handshake integration and unit tests.
- 2026-03-27: run blue/green simulation with synthetic tenants in staging.
- 2026-04-07: limited canary roll to non-P0 tenants.
- 2026-04-15: targeted P0 tenant canary if metrics stable.

Owners: Marcus Li (implementation lead), Aisha Patel (release engineering PM), Diego Ramirez (autoscaler), Linh Tran (observability).
comments: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting notes added. Agreed on TTL-limited reservations and leader-elected coordinator. Action: Marcus to prototype reservation ledger by 2026-03-10.

2026-03-08: Prototype ledger implemented. Discovered conflict window when two SUI leaders in HA attempt same reservations; addressed via optimistic concurrency with revision token. Open: persistence schema migration planning.

2026-03-10: Autoscaler team (Diego) scoped handshake contract. Autoscaler will accept a 'soft-reserve' hint and respond with a boolean 'cannot-reserve' in edge cases. Marcus to add secondary path for reordering waves.
2026-03-12: Integration smoke in staging: 2-node wave completed with synthetic traffic; observed 6% p95 latency bump for a dense tenant. Action: tune reservation sizing down 15% and re-run sim.
2026-03-13: PM asked to include audit trail for gate overrides. Added to backlog; low implementation effort. Planning to surface in next patch.

2026-03-13: Blocking: Confluence doc requires security review for reservation API because it touches tenant identifiers. Set security_review_required to true in ticket checklist (will route separately).
